title: How to look at your data — Jeff Huber (Chroma) + Jason Liu (567)
talk_summary: Chroma and Jason Liu argue that systematic measurement of retrieval inputs (fast golden-set evals) and agent outputs (LLM-extracted structured metadata, clustering, KPI comparison across segments) is what makes product improvement deterministic rather than guesswork. The core mechanism is cheap, fast, repeatable evals plus segment-level analysis to decide what to fix, build, or ignore.

takeaways.technique: Fast golden-set retrieval evals instead of LLM-judge suites
takeaways.what_they_do: Build a set of query→expected-document pairs and measure recall@k for each candidate embedding/retrieval config; runs in seconds for pennies so many experiments are cheap.
takeaways.evidence_quote: all of these metrics should run extremely quickly for pennies
takeaways.numbers: LLM-judge alternative cited as costing $600 and taking three hours to run

takeaways.technique: Synthetic queries aligned to real-query specificity
takeaways.what_they_do: When real queries are scarce, use an LLM taught to write questions whose specificity is semantically aligned to real user queries, avoiding overly-clean benchmark-style questions that inflate scores.
takeaways.evidence_quote: It's too easy to trick yourself into thinking that your system's working really well with synthetic queries that are overly specific to your data.

takeaways.technique: Empirically pick models on your own data, not public benchmarks
takeaways.what_they_do: Run the same fast eval across candidate models and pick by measured recall on your data; found the MTEB-favored model underperformed the actually-best one for their app.
takeaways.numbers: text-embedding-3-small performed worst of four evaluated; MTEB-strong model underperformed for the app

takeaways.technique: Extract structured metadata from agent runs, then cluster and compare KPIs by segment
takeaways.what_they_do: Run each conversation/run through an LLM to extract summary, tools used, errors, satisfaction/frustration; embed and cluster; compare eval KPIs across clusters to find where to invest.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we can build this portfolio of metadata that we can extract. And then what we can do is we can embed this find clusters identify segments

takeaways.technique: Impact-weighted 2x2 (usage vs performance) to decide fix/build/ignore
takeaways.what_they_do: Cross usage frequency with eval performance per segment: high-usage/low-performance is the must-fix; low-usage/low-performance may be a one-line prompt refusal.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If a large portion of your population are using tools that you are bad at, that is clearly the thing you have to fix.

takeaways.technique: Monitor KPI per category over time rather than one aggregate number
takeaways.what_they_do: Track eval metrics broken out by query category over time; a flat 0.5 is meaningless but a category trend reveals product/usage shifts.
takeaways.evidence_quote: where 0.5 doesn't really mean anything but whether or not a metric changes over time across a certain category can determine a lot
